Connectivity among SAARC nations
*241. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India has pledged to upgrade
connectivity among SAARC nations;
(b) whether India has assured SAARC
nations that fast action would be initiated
from 1st April, 2007 by making it easier
for access to roads and transport;
(c) what other assurances were given
by Government at the Second SAARC
Business Leaders Conclave, recently;

agreed to cooperate; and

SAARC nations in this regard?
Brahmaputra Inland Waterways
*242. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the time-frame for completion of
Talweg Surveys, dredging, etc. for
implementation of Brahmaputra Inland
Waterways in view of his D.O.
NO.F20019/5/2007-MT dated 30.1.2007;
(b) the percentage of works already
completed in view of the two years' time-
frame fixed by IWAI for making National
Waterways fully functional; and
(c) whether Government would
consider to constitute a monitoring body
with the elected representatives of Assam
and West Bengal?
Construction of flyover at Badarpur
border
*243. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN
SINGH: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the construction of a
proposed flyover to be built at T-junction
of Delhi-Faridabad-Jaitpur village
(Badarpur border) at National Highway;

78
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) the names of Government and Non-
Government agencies involved therein;
(c) the proposed date of start of
construction of the said project and the
projected period of completion; and
(d) the strategies evolved to complete
the proposed project in stipulated
time?
Concern over use of weapons
in space
†*244. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are concerned
over use of weapons in space;
(b) if so, the measures being taken by
Government for shielding against such
weapons; and
(c) whether there is any proposal for
carrying out deliberations in this regard with
other countries?
Setting up of National Science and
Social Science Foundation
*245. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
MS. MABEL REBELLO:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
view on the recommendation of National
Knowledge Commission regarding setting
up of a National Science and Social Science
Foundation (NS3F);
(b) if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) if so, the details of the mandate of
NS3F;
(d) what would be the linkages of the
new Foundation with the existing network
of the research institutions in science and
social science; and
(e) in what manner Government
propose to avoid overlap in mandates?
Issuance of OCI cards
†*246. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS
INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of OCI cards issued as
on date under the Overseas Citizenship of
India scheme;
(b) the details thereof, country-wise;
(c) whether Government are planning
to formulate any scheme to give special
facilities to the OCI card holders; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Expenditure pattern under Central
schemes
*247. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the expenditure pattern under the
Central schemes during the Financial Year
2006-07, quarter-wise;
(b) the break-up of revenue and capital
expenditures under the Central schemes;

79
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) whether it is a fact that the allocations
under the Central schemes have not been
spent evenly through the Financial Year;
(d) the schemes that have not been able
to use even half of the funds till December,
2006, Ministry-wise details thereof; and
(e) the steps that are being taken for a
more efficient and even utilization of funds
of Central schemes?
Pilgrimage cities under JNNURM
†*248. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether any scheme has been
formulated for the development of famous
pilgrimage cities under the Jawaharlal Nehru
National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM);
(b) if so, the cities included under this
scheme; and
(c) the comprehensive details thereof?
Obscene pictures and information in
websites
†*249. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that several cyber
cafes are misusing internet services by
putting obscene pictures and informations
in websites;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
one website had recently shown obscene
picture of Mahatma Gandhi;
(c) whether Government would take
some steps to check misuse of websites
and cyber crimes as well; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Joint venture for Titanium based
industry
*250. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Government of Andhra Pradesh has entered
into MoU with Bothli STARK Company
for a joint venture for establishing Titanium
based industry (extracting of mining of
beach sand) in the East Coast of the State
(Srikakulam to Vizag);
(b) if so, whether Government have
given necessary clearances/permissions to
A.P. Government to enter into a MoU with
Bothli STARK for joint venture; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government had earlier rejected permission
to Andhra Pradesh Mining Development
Corporation for mining the beach sand
because it is deterimental to the existence
of Olive Ridley Tortoise?
Turnover of BSNL
*251. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Ltd. is considering to double
its turnover to US dollar 20 billion in the
next three years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that BSNL
is also making efforts for network
upgradation and capacity building; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

80
Deficiencies in Master Plan 2021
†*252. SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have approved
the proposed Master Plan 2021 for Delhi
which carries a lot of deficiencies;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) if not, the details thereof?
Growth rate target for Eleventh Plan
*253. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the GDP of the country
registered growth rates of 7.5 per cent and
8.4 per cent during the years 2004-05 and
2005-06 respectively;
(b) if so, the complete details thereof,
year-wise and sector-wise;
(c) the target and expected growth rate
of 2006-07, sector-wise;
(d) the steps Government are taking to
achieve more growth rate in the Eleventh
Five Year Plan in each sector; and
(e) the steps being taken by
Government to boost each sector to achieve
a good growth rate?
Atomic Power Project, Koodankulam
*254. SHRI K.P.K. KUMARAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Power Allocation
Formula in the matter of I and II Reactors
of the Koodankulam Atomic Power Project
be modified as a special case to help the
natural resourceless State of Tamil Nadu;
(b) whether any requests regarding the
unallocated residual power of 300 M.W.
have been received from the Southern
States; and
(c) whether the entire quantum of this
unallocated power would be allocated to
Tamil Nadu since people of the State are
completely dissatisfied with the 925 M.W.
earmarked for the State out of the total
production of 2000 M.W.?
Privatisation of coal production
†*255. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have entrusted
the mining of coal exclusively to the private
companies;
(b) whether Government have started
privatisation of various parts of the process
of coal production; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Regulatory Authority for Higher
Education
*256. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether, seeking reforms in the
present education system, the National
Knowledge Commission has urged Prime
Minister to intiate a move to establish an
independent Regulatory Authority for
Higher Education;
(b) if so, whether in a letter to the Prime
Minister, NKC Chairman has pointed out
that the present regulatory system in higher
education is flawed in some important
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

81
respects and the barriers to entry are too
high; and
(c) if so, the steps being considered by
the Prime Minister in this regard?
Vacancies of OBC category
*257. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 27 per cent
quota earmarked for filling up vacancies of
OBC category has never been filled in the
All India Civil Services examination in the
twelve years since it was implemented;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and if not,
the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the short-
fall has been steadily growing; and
(d) if so, the steps taken to fill up the
entire quota of 27 per cent earmarked for
them by Government?
Four-laning of NH-17 in Goa
*258. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the work on the four-laning
of National Highway 17 from Patradevi in
North Goa to Polen in South Goa has
commenced;
(b) if not, the stage at which the project
lies; and
(c) the reasons for the delay in
implementing the project?
FDI hike in telecom sector
*259. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to with-hold its decision to hike FDI in
telecom to 74 per cent;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether the security concern arising
from increase in FDI was the main reason?
Inland Water Transport
*260. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that presently
nearly 9 per cent of our rivers are used for
navigational purposes despite India having
world's largest number of rivers, canals and
lakes being available for inland water
transport;
(b) if so, keeping in view that cost of
development of inland water network is
less than 10 per cent of constructing a
similar multilane road link, the reasons for
14,500 km navigable waterways not being
adequately used; and
(c) the annual financial outlay for such
projects during the Tenth Five Year Plan
and whether these funds were spent?

Availability of Uranium for nuclear
energy plant
†1797. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to increase the availability of Uranium for
utilization of atomic energy for peaceful
purposes and also for generating electricity
following Indo-American Nuclear
Agreement; and
(b) if so, the details of efforts made by
Government for making available the fuel
for nuclear energy plants?
 Uranium mines to private sector
1798. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to give
Uranium mines to the private sector for
mining and processing;
(b) if so, the mines which Government
propose to privatize and the reasons
therefor;
(c) for how many years this contract
would be given and the quantity they would
process;
(d) whom they would sell the finished
Uranium; and
(e) how Government would ensure
safety in the Uranium processing?
 PPP model for exploration of
Uranium oxide
1799. SHRI DARA SINGH:
SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that our country
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

of 1,17,800 metric tonnes;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to have a Private Public Partnership (PPP)

the Uranium Corporation of India Ltd.
(UCIL);

(d) the steps Government have taken so
far to set up/operate viable projects in this
regard?
 Review of availability of Uranium
1800. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to initiate a complete review of the
availability of Uranium to fuel its nuclear
power plants in the wake of the successful
culmination of the Indo-US agreement for
peaceful use of nuclear power;
(b) whether India is likely to acquire
economically viable Uranium deposits
abroad to exploit them for peaceful
domestic use, apart from setting up new
Uranium exploration and extraction projects
in six States; and

contained in a presentation by the
Department of Atomic Energy to the
Committee of Secretaries in December,
2006?
 Signing of CTBT

state:
(a) whether both domestic and foreign
private companies have submitted their
proposals in the nuclear power sector;
(b) if so, the names of such major
companies and the countries they belong to;
(c) whether India is going to allow entry
to all the companies of international repute

coal production is made through contractors

(b) if so, whether laws of the land permit
this in coal mines production;

Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased

E-auction of coal;
(b) whether Government have evolved
an alternative mechanism to allocate coal;

only for dumping by CMPDI;

company; and

UHV so that it does not remain fit for sale;

situated at Gevra Dipika, which is a barell
washery, can produce over 65 per cent of
ash and whether any enquiry into the same

authority; and

companies

of the requirement of coal for steel
companies is being met through import;

during the last three years, year-wise;
(c) whether desired results have not
been achieved inspite of allowing private
agencies in coal mining sector; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor and the
steps Government are taking to increase
the production of coal?

mines; and

to other industries?

could earn their livelihood legally;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the view-point of Government in this
regard?

$80 billion export target for the IT sector to
be achieved by 2010; and
(e) if so, the details of the roadmap drawn
for achieving this target?

06 the Minister of Finance had promised to
give telephone connectivity to the remaining

two years of Bharat Nirman against a target
of 66,822 villages?

 DR. MURLI MANOHAR

 DR. MURLI MANOHAR

SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:

BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of

pleased to state:
(a) whether in a bid to cut down losses
and achieve a higher degree of
competitiveness, the Department of Posts
has put together an ambitious action plan
to connect most of its major post offices
across the country and is planning to invest
Rs. 6,000 crore for the technology
upgradation across its postal network;

to enhance its technology to compete with
the private players; and

plans to invest Rs. 12,000 crore during the

computerize and connect its 1.5 lakh post

conductor policy has been delayed in view
of differences between Ministry of Finance

30 per cent subsidy is provided on semi
conductor project cost; and

(a) whether there has been degradation

service providers;
